model: Sum-of-parts owner-FCF DCF: Energy Markets flows plus tax-grossed APLNG distributions on a PV-equivalent taper, Octopus and Kraken stakes in the equity bridge (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Octopus Energy equity-accounted investment (22.7% economic interest, ex-Kraken) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: FY26 annual note B.3: carrying amount $1,213m at 30 June 2026. Held at book, not marked up: the retained Octopus retail/services business is near break-even for Origin's share (FY26 -$8m EBITDA, FY25 -$88m) and its FY26 EBITDA share is excluded from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Kraken Technologies direct stake at fair value
equity_bridge.note: Carried at only $270m (allocated historical goodwill), but the demerger accounting eliminated a $2,003m fair-value gain on the shares distributed to Origin, and Octopus's own retained 15.3% is carried at fair value A$1,808m (implying ~A$11.8bn for 100% of Kraken; Origin's ~19-20% direct interest ~A$2.2-2.3bn). Valued at ~$2.2bn. At carrying value only (1,483 total for both stakes) the weighted IV would be ~$1.1/share lower. The bridge is scenario-independent by construction; Kraken's licensing growth (>20%/yr) is the unmodelled upside and a down-round the unmodelled downside.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY27 Energy Markets guidance is flat on FY26 at the midpoint; long-run nominal revenue growth set to ~2.5% (inflation plus electrification volume) rather than any historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (0.6%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (5.2%) and EPS: FY21-FY22 carried $3.7bn of statutory losses (APLNG impairments, derivative fair-value losses) and dividends have since paid out ~50% of Adjusted FCF, so book value is not the compounding base. Revenue CAGRs are wholesale-price pass-through (FY23 peak $16.5bn, FY26 $15.6bn), not volume. EPS 5-yr is null because FY21 EPS was negative (-$1.30).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not a usable growth anchor for Origin: the 3-yr figure (FY23 owner FCF ~$0.6bn including the $1,783m APLNG dividend against -$633m OCF, to FY26 ~$1.8bn) is a working-capital and futures-collateral artefact of the 2022-23 wholesale price spike, and pre-FY23 APLNG dividends are not in the KPI table, so the 5-yr figure is null. Growth is set from guidance and the component build.

scenario_narratives.base: Energy Markets delivers the FY27 guidance midpoint ($1.7bn EBITDA) as the battery portfolio ramps against lower wholesale tariffs, then compounds ~3% a year; APLNG distributions step down to ~$850m and taper with field decline; LNG trading gains normalise; Octopus is held at carrying value and Kraken at its demerger fair value. Value is roughly 50% Energy Markets, 35% APLNG and 15% Octopus/Kraken before net debt.
scenario_narratives.bull: Firming premiums, electrification volume growth, cost-out and an accretive Eraring extension lift Energy Markets to ~$1.8bn growing 4.5%; oil in the US$75-85 range and APLNG optimisation hold distributions near $950m with slower decline. Kraken upside beyond demerger fair value is not in the number.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulatory price intervention, post-breach churn and the loss of Eraring's firming margin hold Energy Markets at the bottom of guidance with ~1% growth; oil at ~US$60 and fast field decline cut APLNG distributions to ~$700m and falling 12% a year; a 13x terminal cap reflects a shrinking asset base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Origin is three businesses with three different cash-flow characters: a stable but capital-hungry integrated retailer/generator, a declining oil-linked LNG annuity, and a minority stake in a growing software business that pays no cash. The model charges each once and only once: Energy Markets on unlevered owner FCF at an AUD WACC; APLNG on its after-tax distributions with the finite life priced through the taper rather than a higher discount rate; Octopus/Kraken as an asset in the bridge with its near-zero EBITDA share stripped from the flows. The result is anchored to the FY27 guidance year and to management's own capex framing, and it deliberately does not credit growth capex with returns it has not yet earned.
key_risks_to_valuation: APLNG distributions: every US$10/bbl on JCC moves Origin's annual distribution by roughly $150-200m, i.e. ~$1/share of PV; FY27 guidance assumptions (US$72 JCC, 0.65 AUD/USD) are the base anchor
Regulatory intervention in retail tariffs (DMO) and east-coast gas (Gas Market Code, ADGSM successor) can compress Energy Markets margins by several hundred million with little notice
Eraring closure (April 2029) and the pace of the battery/renewables build determine whether Energy Markets margins hold; management calls large-scale renewables economics 'very challenging'
Octopus/Kraken bridge value ($3.4bn, ~$2.0/share) rests on the June 2026 demerger fair value; a down-round or Octopus retail losses would cut it, and the bridge does not vary by scenario
Growth capex above the modelled 4.5% of revenue (Yanco Delta ~$4bn at 100%) without matching EBITDA would reduce value; conversely the model gives no credit for CIS-underwritten returns on it
July 2026 data breach (~900,000 accounts): OAIC penalties, remediation cost and churn are unquantified and sit only in the bear weight

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 10.02-12.99
data_sources.financials: ORG.AX_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2026 annuals, H1 FY2019-H1 FY2026 halves) plus ORG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt: Underlying Profit reconciliation (section 4.2), segment Underlying EBITDA and cash-flow table (section 4.3), statutory cash flow statement, note D.5 net debt, note B.3/Octopus-Kraken demerger note, note G.6 OCF reconciliation, EPS note (diluted shares)
data_sources.qualitative: ORG.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24): FY27 guidance (Energy Markets EBITDA $1,550-1,850m, APLNG production 625-670 PJ, APLNG capex/opex $3.0-3.3bn, Origin capex $450-650m), risks, bull/bear cases

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note G.6 (OCF reconciliation) 'Share-based payment expense' 46 (FY25: 36). No equity-award tax withholding line: awards are satisfied by on-market purchases (4.0m shares bought for employee plans in FY26, ~$45m at the average price), so the expense and the cash cost coincide. Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is empty for every period; this is the filing figure.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026, note on EPS (1,725,741,266); 1,719.9m on issue excluding treasury shares. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and Origin neutralises award dilution with on-market purchases (count 1,717.6m -> 1,719.9m over two years). No buy-back is in place (annual report: 'no current on-market buy-back').
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, single rate for all scenarios (risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate). AUD 10-year government bond ~4.3%, ERP 5.5%, equity beta 0.9 for an integrated energy retailer/generator -> cost of equity ~9.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (FY26 interest and transaction costs $239m on ~$4.0bn average borrowings), 3.9% after 30% tax. Market weights at the valuation date: equity ~$19.0bn, borrowings ex-leases net of cash ~$3.7bn -> ~16% debt -> ~8.4%. Rounded to 8.5% because roughly 40% of near-term cash flow is the oil/JCC-linked APLNG distribution, which deserves a higher rate than a pure retailer; the taper on that stream (see notes) is the other place the finite, declining nature of APLNG is charged. Not stacked with any further premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The full cash lease payment (FY26: $85m principal in financing + $30m lease interest inside 'interest and transaction costs' = $115m, 0.74% of revenue) is charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, rising to ~1.0% of revenue as the Supernode battery tolling agreements (lease liabilities $504m -> $1,175m at 30 June 2026) reach a full year. Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: total_debt = borrowings only $3,811m (total interest-bearing liabilities $4,986m less lease liabilities $1,175m). Metrics.csv TotalDebt of 4,986 includes leases and is not the bridge figure. D&A path (3.8-4.0% of revenue) is Origin's own $579m underlying D&A which includes right-of-use depreciation of roughly $85m; with lease cash charged in EBITDA, a small double count of ROU depreciation remains inside the tax line only (EBIT understated by ~0.5% of revenue before tax), which is conservative and immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are nil (FY26 NCI share of Underlying Profit $0m); no deduction.
inputs.equity_accounted_treatment: APLNG (27.5%) and Octopus Energy / Kraken Technologies (22.7% combined economic interest) are EQUITY-ACCOUNTED, not proportionally consolidated. Underlying EBITDA of $3,220m includes Origin's share of APLNG EBITDA ($1,478m) and of Octopus EBITDA (-$8m), both non-cash (reversed in the OCF reconciliation, note G.6). The only cash from APLNG is the dividend ($911m FY26, $797m FY25), booked in INVESTING activities and therefore absent from Metrics.csv OperatingCashFlow/FreeCashFlow. The model builds cash EBITDA per year as: Energy Markets EBITDA + Integrated Gas Other (Origin's own LNG trading, Cameron contract) + Corporate + SBC add-back + APLNG distributions grossed up at the 30% cash tax rate (so that after the engine's tax line they net back to the after-tax, fully franked distribution). Octopus and Kraken are excluded from the flows and carried in the equity bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.apl_ng_taper_note: APLNG is a finite, declining asset (FY26 production 668 PJ, FY27 guidance 625-670 PJ; capex/opex guided up to $3.0-3.3bn; LNG SPAs run to the mid-2030s, 2P reserves to roughly the mid-2040s). A perpetuity terminal on year-10 cash flow would capitalise the tail at ~15-17x. To be PV-equivalent, the explicit APLNG distribution path in the base case declines ~10% a year nominal from $850m in FY27 (bull ~8% from $950m, bear ~12% from $700m), which at 8.5% reproduces the present value of a stream that declines ~4% a year to FY2045 and then stops (~A$6.1bn base). The grossed-up APLNG line therefore drives most of the EBITDA-margin decline across the horizon; the Energy Markets margin itself is broadly stable.
inputs.notes: Model: Sum-of-parts inside the owner-FCF component engine (fresh build, no prior valuation, no MEMORY.md entry). Routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical (oil-linked JV cash, wholesale power prices) -> owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency, leases B, NCI nil, matching-asset rule for the equity-accounted stakes, SBC-light market, risk charged once). Three streams: (1) Energy Markets + Corporate + Integrated Gas Other in the flows; (2) APLNG 27.5% distributions in the flows, tax-grossed and tapered (see apl_ng_taper_note); (3) Octopus Energy at its $1,213m equity-accounted carrying value and the direct Kraken Technologies stake at ~$2,200m fair value in the equity bridge. Net debt is borrowings ($3,811m) less Origin's own cash ($113m: $307m reported less $194m held as APLNG upstream operator to fund APLNG operations, per note D.5). The $210m Kraken equity-raise investment in July 2026 is post balance date and debt-funded (asset and debt both up ~$210m at cost) and is left out of both sides. FY26 owner FCF of $1,797m (reported 1,859 = OCF 1,917 - capex 969 + APLNG dividends 911; less SBC 46 and interest received 16) is flattered by a $158m cash-tax trough (FY25: $767m), a $125m futures-collateral inflow and $100m of Queensland Government funds received in advance; the component build's year-1 owner FCF of ~$1.55bn sits deliberately below it. Cash tax rate is held at 30% in every scenario because the APLNG gross-up only nets correctly at that rate; Origin's own underlying effective rate is ~28%. Interest income ($16m received) is stripped by convention; with $3.7bn net debt there is no cash pile to double count. Working capital capture is zero: FY26 receivables/payables/collateral swings of several hundred million are wholesale-price and margining noise, not growth-linked. Buyback_cash is 0 (on-market purchases of $109m fund employee plans and the DRP, not a capital return).
inputs.adjusted_fcf_reconciliation: Origin's own Adjusted Free Cash Flow FY26 $2,074m = statutory OCF 1,917 + investing -63 (which already includes the $911m APLNG dividend) - interest 239 + major growth capex 484 + Qld funds 100 - collateral 125. The model's unlevered owner FCF adds back interest and does not add back growth capex.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Energy Markets $1,560m FY27 (bottom of guidance) growing 1%/yr; Integrated Gas Other $20m; Corporate -$100m growing 2.5%; SBC add-back 0.3%; APLNG distributions $700m FY27 (JCC ~US$60, stronger AUD, capex/opex at the top of the $3.0-3.3bn range) grossed up to $1,000m and declining 12%/yr. Year 1: 2,524 / 14,791 = 17.06%; year 10: 1,969 / 17,417 = 11.30%. Terminal cap 13x.
bear.narrative: Cost-of-living intervention (DMO caps, gas code) compresses retail margins, the July 2026 data breach lifts churn and brings OAIC penalties, Eraring's 2029 closure removes owned firming capacity and squeezes the retail hedge, and Yanco Delta is either abandoned or built at sub-WACC returns. Oil settles around US$60 and APLNG field decline runs at the fast end, cutting distributions below $500m within five years. The Octopus/Kraken bridge is unchanged, which flatters this case if Kraken's next raise is a down-round.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Cash EBITDA per year = Energy Markets EBITDA (FY27 $1,700m, guidance midpoint of $1,550-1,850m, then +3%/yr on battery ramp, VPP and cost-to-serve, net of Eraring's April 2029 closure) + Integrated Gas Other $60m flat ('modest LNG trading gains' guided for FY27/FY28 vs $142m FY26) + Corporate -$95m growing 2.5%/yr + SBC add-back 0.3% of revenue + APLNG distributions grossed up at 30% ($850m FY27 -> /0.7 = $1,214m, declining 10%/yr nominal). Year 1: 2,924 / 15,102 = 19.36%; year 10: 2,685 / 18,768 = 14.31%. Energy Markets alone is ~11.3% of revenue in year 1 and ~11.8% in year 10.
base.capex_note: FY27 capex guided $450-650m (maintain/sustain 200-300, growth 250-350): 3.6% of FY27 revenue. From FY28, 4.5% of revenue (~$700m rising to ~$850m) = sustaining plus a continuing battery/renewables program; Yanco Delta (~$4bn, FID targeted mid-FY27 with partners, economics 'very challenging' per management) is not separately charged because the engine gives no EBITDA credit for it either.
base.narrative: Energy Markets holds guidance-midpoint EBITDA in FY27 as battery ramp-up offsets lower wholesale tariffs, then grows ~3% a year. APLNG distributions step down to ~$850m in FY27 (production -3%, capex/opex +5%, JCC ~US$70) and are tapered for the finite field life. LNG trading gains normalise to 'modest'. Octopus and Kraken are held at carrying and demerger fair value respectively.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Energy Markets $1,800m FY27 (upper half of guidance) growing 4.5%/yr; Integrated Gas Other $100m; Corporate -$95m growing 2.5%; SBC add-back 0.3%; APLNG distributions $950m FY27 (JCC ~US$80, AUD ~0.65) grossed up to $1,357m and declining 8%/yr. Year 1: 3,208 / 15,258 = 21.03%; year 10: 3,357 / 19,908 = 16.86%.
bull.narrative: Firming and battery premiums land as coal exits the NEM, electrification and data-centre load lift volumes, cost-to-serve savings hold, and the Eraring extension is earnings-accretive; oil-linked LNG pricing stays in the US$75-85 range and APLNG optimisation slows decline to ~2%/yr. Kraken's >20% licensing growth is still only in the bridge at demerger fair value, so the bull case is understated on that axis by design.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear weight is raised from 15% because two of Origin's largest value drivers are outside its control and two-sided: JCC-linked APLNG pricing and government intervention in east-coast gas and retail tariffs, and a live cyber-breach liability sits on top. Bull weight is cut from 35% because the bull case needs oil, firming premiums and Yanco Delta returns to line up independently, and the Kraken upside that would justify a heavier bull weight is deliberately carried in the bridge rather than in the scenario.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
